topic: What antenna aperture size trade-offs exist between LEO and GEO satellites when optimizing gain and portability for CMOS-based ground terminals?
consensus_response: The selection of frequency bands impacts antenna aperture size trade-offs between LEO and GEO satellites. Higher frequencies (e.g., Ka-band) are more susceptible to atmospheric effects, while lower frequencies (e.g., S-band) require larger apertures due to increased path loss. Phased array antennas can mitigate these trade-offs by enabling flexible designs and reducing interference susceptibility. In LEO systems, smaller antenna apertures can lead to increased interference susceptibility due to the shorter distances to the ground, resulting in reduced capacity and higher latency. In contrast, GEO satellites require larger apertures to compensate for the longer distances, increasing complexity but providing higher gain and better signal quality.
